Let me analyze this OIML certificate for water meters.

Key details:
- Certificate number: R49/2013-A-CZ1-2021.07, Revision 1
- Scheme A
- Member State: Czech Republic
- Issuing Authority: Czech Metrology Institute, Okružní 31, 638 00 Brno, Czech Republic
- Person responsible: Jan Kalandra
- Applicant: George Kent (Malaysia) Berhad, Lot 1115, Jalan Puchong; Taman Meranti Jaya; 47120 Puchong, Selangor, Malaysia
- Manufacturer: George Kent (Malaysia) Berhad (same address)
- Certified type: water meter – positive displacement, dry dial; types GKMV40, GKMV40P
- Module designation: "-" → Not applicable
- Recommendation: OIML R 49, Edition 2013
- Accuracy class: 2
- Date issued: 27 September 2022 (signed date on revision 1). The certificate history shows Addition 0 issued 6 December 2021, Addition 1 27 September 2022. The date_issued should probably be 2022-09-27 (the signature date). Original: 2021-12-06.
- page_total: 7

Issuing authority details:
- Name: Czech Metrology Institute
- Address: Okružní 31, 638 00 Brno, Czech Republic
- Person responsible: Jan Kalandra
- Also RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body (signatory). Hmm — "person_responsible" field: page 1 says "Person responsible: Jan Kalandra". The signature is by Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body. I'll use Jan Kalandra as person_responsible, and maybe include person_title? The schema has person_responsible and person_title. The signature block says "The OIML Issuing Authority RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body". I think person_responsible = Jan Kalandra; person_title — not clearly stated for Jan Kalandra. Could include signatory info. I'll set person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra" and omit person_title or set to "Head of Certification Body"? The title belongs to Klenovský. Safer: person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra", omit person_title. Or note signature. Schema allows only those fields. I'll omit person_title.

Test reports:
- OIML type evaluation No. 0511-ER-V114-21 dated 22 October 2021, 23 pages including annex 1 → role: type_evaluation_report
- Test report No. 6015-PT-P5009-21, 67 pages including annex 1 → role: test_report
- No 0511-ERV056-22 dated 27 September 2022, 29 pages including annex 1 → role: evaluation_report
- Documentation file: 0511-UL-V056-22 → role: documentation_file

Revision history:
- Addition 0, 6 December 2021, "Issuing certificate"
- Addition 1, 27 September 2022, "Added sizes DN20, DN25 and GKMV40-Sensors and Sealing"

Revision as string: "0" and "1".

Models: GKMV40 and GKMV40P, each in DN15, DN20, DN25 sizes. The characteristics table has three columns (15, 20, 25 nominal diameters).

Model family: models could be identified by combination. The table columns are per nominal diameter (DN15, DN20, DN25). Body type: brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P). So there are effectively 2 types × 3 sizes = 6 variants. But the characteristics table is per-size.

I'll set model_family with models keyed by DN size, since attributes vary per DN. But the type GKMV40 vs GKMV40P differ only in body material. Hmm. Options:
- models: ["DN15", "DN20", "DN25"] and model_level attributes per size.
- Also record GKMV40 vs GKMV40P as type_designations on certified_type.

I think the cleanest: model_family.family_name: null, models: [{model_id: "DN15"}, {model_id: "DN20"}, {model_id: "DN25"}] with attributes: for DN15: q1, q2, q3, q4, indicating_range, resolution, reed sensor connection etc. But the GKMV40/GKMV40P distinction... maybe model_id "GKMV40 DN15" etc. would be 6 models. The attributes table is only per DN, so values would repeat for the two body variants. I'll go with 6 models? That could be overkill. Alternatively, models per DN with attributes including body_material: "brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P)".

Hmm. Actually let me think about which is more useful. The certificate covers types GKMV40 and GKMV40P. The distinguishing characteristic is body material. Size variants DN15/DN20/DN25 have different flow values. The R60 example uses model_id like "Emax=25t". For R137 uses "G1.6", "G2.5" size identifiers. Following R137, model_id per size: "DN15", "DN20", "DN25". That's simpler and matches the table. The type designations GKMV40, GKMV40P are on certified_type.type_designations.

But then body material difference — could be a type_level characteristic: body_material: "brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P)". Or components? It's not a component per se.

I'll go with models = DN15, DN20, DN25, and type-level notes for body variants. Actually, maybe model entries could include attributes: {body_material_variants: ["brass", "composite"]}? Keep simple: models [{model_id: "GKMV40 DN15"}, ...]? Hmm.

Let me decide: models keyed "DN15", "DN20", "DN25" — because the characteristics matrix is by nominal diameter. The two type designations (GKMV40 brass, GKMV40P composite) apply to all sizes. I'll add type_level characteristic body_material with string value "brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P)". Actually a cleaner way: certified_type.description covers it.

Model-level matrix from the table:

Nominal diameter [mm]: 15, 20, 25
Q1 [m³/h]: 0.0063, 0.01, 0.0158
Q2 [m³/h]: 0.0100, 0.016, 0.0252
Q3 [m³/h]: 2.50, 4.0, 6.30
Q4 [m³/h]: 3.13, 5.0, 7.88
Indicating range [m³]: "9999 or 99 999", "99 999", "99 999" — hmm, this is odd; for DN15 it's 9999 or 99999, others 99999. Value: for DN15 it's two options. I can record as string "9999 or 99999"? Or list. Schema value can be a string. I'll use string "9999 or 99999" for DN15 and number 99999 for DN20/DN25? Mixed types in one attribute's values are okay since each value object is separate. For DN15: {"value": "9999 or 99999"}. Hmm, or treat as list of numbers — but the schema says value is number | {min,max} | string. String is fine.

Resolution of the indicating device [m³]: "0.000002 or 0.00002", 0.00002, 0.00002. Same approach: string for DN15.

Resolution of the device for rapid testing [dm³]: 156.6, 89.7, 47.49.

Type-level characteristics:
- q3_over_q1_ratio: 400 (Q₃/Q₁)
- q2_over_q1_ratio: 1.6 (Q₂/Q₁)
- q3_over_q4_ratio: 1.25 (Q₃/Q₄) — note normally Q4/Q3 = 1.25; the table says Q₃/Q₄: 1.25. I'll keep as given: q3_over_q4_ratio... actually the value 1.25 = Q4/Q3 conventionally. The table labels it "Q₃/Q₄". Hmm, Q3/Q4 = 2.5/3.13 = 0.8. So the label is likely a typo for Q4/Q3. But rule: don't fabricate/correct. I'll label `q3_over_q4_ratio` with value 1.25? That's misleading but faithful. Or label `q4_over_q3_ratio`? Faithful extraction: keep the label as in the doc: "Q₃/Q₄" → q3_over_q4_ratio. Hmm. Actually, canonical label rule says use snake_case canonical labels. The document says Q₃/Q₄. I'll keep q3_over_q4_ratio value 1.25. Alternatively name it `q4_over_q3` — no, stay faithful.

- measuring_principle: "positive displacement"
- accuracy_class: 2
- mpe_lower_zone: ±5 % → value: -5 to 5? It's "±5 %". Could be value: 5, unit "%", with sign? Typically I'd record as {min: -5, max: 5}, unit "%". Or value "±5". I'll use {min: -5, max: 5}, unit_symbol "%".
- mpe_upper_zone: ±2 % for water ≤ 30 °C; ±3 % for > 30 °C → config_level with axis "water_temperature". Values: {condition: "water temperature ≤ 30 °C", value: 2, unit_symbol: "%"} and {condition: "water temperature > 30 °C", value: 3, unit_symbol: "%"}. Value ±2: I'll use 2 with magnitude. Hmm, structured value must be number; ±2 as {min:-2,max:2}? For config values, keep consistent: value: 2. Actually "maximum permissible error ±2 %" — error limits are ±. I'll use {min: -2, max: 2}. Let me be consistent: MPE values as range -x..x. For mpe_lower_zone: {min:-5, max:5}. For config: {min:-2,max:2} and {min:-3,max:3}. That's fine.

- temperature_class: "T30 or T50" → string value "T30 or T50". Or list. I'll use string.
- water_pressure_class: "MAP 16" → string "MAP 16".
- pressure_loss_class: "ΔP 63" → string "ΔP 63" or "ΔP 63". Avoid Δ? It's a symbol, fine. Use "ΔP 63".
- environmental_class: "B, O" → string "B, O". Footnote marker 1) — the sup is "1" for Environmental class. footnote_markers: ["1)"]. The footnote definitions: superscript 1: "Valid for water meter with an electronic device; if it is equipped, these classes are set in combination with parameters of ancillary device. Information specified by the manufacturer." and superscript 2: "Ancillary devices – reed sensor and inductive sensor – have not been tested."

footnotes[]: marker "1)" text..., marker "2)" text....

- electromagnetic_environment: "E1", footnote_markers ["1)"]
- mechanical_class: "M1", footnote_markers ["1)"]
- maximum_admissible_temperature: 50, unit "°C"
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6, unit "MPa"
- orientation_limitation: "any"
- connection_type: per DN: G¾”B, G1”B, G1 ¼ ”B → model_level attribute connection_type: values "G¾\"B", "G1\"B", "G1 ¼\"B". These are strings (thread designations). I could put in model_level since varies per model: attribute "connection_type_screw_thread", values: [{model: DN15, value: "G¾B"}, ...]. The inch marks: G¾”B → "G3/4\"B"? Use "G¾”B" as given? Keep as string "G¾”B". Maybe normalize to "G3/4 B"? I'll keep as in doc: "G¾”B". Hmm, JSON supports unicode fine.

Actually should connection be model_level or matrix_table? It varies per DN — model_level works.

- minimum_straight_length_inlet_pipe: 0 mm
- minimum_straight_length_outlet_pipe: 0 mm
- flow_conditioner: "No"
- mounting: "in line meter"
- orientation: "any"
- eut_category: "Positive displacement water meters"
- eut_case: "A"
- reed_sensor_power_supply: "max. 48 V DC/AC / 50 mA" → split: reed_sensor_max_supply_voltage: {min: null, max: 48}, unit "V"; reed_sensor_supply_type: "DC/AC"; reed_sensor_max_supply_current: {max: 50}, unit "mA". footnote_markers ["2)"].
- inductive_sensor_power_supply: max 24 V DC / 20 mA → inductive_sensor_max_supply_voltage: {max: 24}, "V"; inductive_sensor_supply_type: "DC"; inductive_sensor_max_supply_current: {max: 20}, "mA". footnote ["2)"].

Type-level for the model attributes: q3/q1 etc.

Model-level entries:
- nominal_diameter: 15/20/25, unit "mm"
- q1: unit m³/h: 0.0063, 0.01, 0.0158
- q2: 0.0100, 0.016, 0.0252
- q3: 2.5, 4.0, 6.3
- q4: 3.13, 5.0, 7.88
- indicating_range: unit m³: "9999 or 99999", 99999, 99999
- indicating_device_resolution: unit m³: "0.000002 or 0.00002", 0.00002, 0.00002
- rapid_testing_device_resolution: unit dm³ (litre): 156.6, 89.7, 47.49
- connection_type: "G¾”B", "G1”B", "G1 ¼”B"
- length: unit mm: 115, 165, 199

matrix_tables: The characteristics table is essentially a matrix — I could emit one matrix_table "Basic technical data" with columns. That might be redundant with model_level but rule 4 R137 example shows both matrix_tables and model_level. I'll include a matrix_table for the main data table:

name: "Basic technical data of water meters types GKMV40 and GKMV40P"
columns: ["nominal_diameter", "q1", "q2", "q3", "q4", "indicating_range", "indicating_device_resolution", "rapid_testing_device_resolution", "connection_type", "length"]
column_units: ["mm", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³", "m³", "dm³", null, "mm"]
rows: [
 {nominal_diameter: 15, q1: 0.0063, q2: 0.01, q3: 2.5, q4: 3.13, indicating_range: "9999 or 99999", indicating_device_resolution: "0.000002 or 0.00002", rapid_testing_device_resolution: 156.6, connection_type: "G¾”B", length: 115},
 {nominal_diameter: 20, ...},
 {nominal_diameter: 25, ...}
]

Wait, but indicating range / resolution columns in original table are in different positions; fine to reorganize.

Components: The water meter consists of body, inlet strainer, volumetric chamber with oscillating piston, magnetic coupling, O-ring, pressure plate, magnetic shields, indicating device, register cap and clamp-on cover. Also ancillary devices: reed sensor, inductive sensor (pulse transmitter). Should I list components? Rule 6: "For complex instruments (e.g. Measuring sensor + Pulser + Calculating device), record each as components[] entry". The cert names sub-assemblies in the description. I could include key components: indicating device (mechanical, 8 drums + 1 pointer), reed sensor (ancillary device, untested), inductive sensor/pulser (ancillary, untested). Figure 3 shows "INDUCTIVE PULSER". I'll include:

components:
- role: "body", type_designations: [], characteristics: {material: ...}? Body material varies by type: brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P). characteristics: {material: "brass or composite"}. Hmm, maybe simpler.
- role: "indicating_device", characteristics: {type: "mechanical, dry dial", drums: 8, pointer: 1}
- role: "ancillary_device_reed_sensor", alternatives? The cert says "If the meter is equipped by the reed impulse transmitter or the inductive transmitter". These are alternatives — alternatives: "OR"? They're separate components either of which may be fitted. I'll add:
  - role: "reed_sensor (pulse transmitter, ancillary device)", type_designations: [], characteristics: {max_supply_voltage: 48 V, supply_type: DC/AC, max_current: 50 mA}, note untested via footnote.
  - role: "inductive_sensor (inductive pulser, ancillary device)", characteristics: {max_supply_voltage: 24 V DC, max_current: 20 mA}.
  alternatives "OR" between reed and inductive? They are each optional. I'll set alternatives "OR" on... hmm, alternatives field describes that components are alternatives. I'll include reed and inductive as separate entries and not force alternatives. Actually rule 6: "When the cert offers alternatives (e.g. Transmitter UMC4 OR UMC4-RM), record alternatives: 'OR'." The reed OR inductive sensor are alternatives. But they're separate roles. I'll just list both without alternatives. Or maybe safer to keep components minimal: indicating device, wet volumetric chamber (oscillating piston), and sensors. Let me include a reasonable set:

components:
1. role: "measuring chamber", characteristics: {type: "wet volumetric chamber with oscillating piston"}
2. role: "indicating device", characteristics: {type: "mechanical, dry dial, numbered rollers", number_of_drums: 8, pointers: 1}
3. role: "body", characteristics: {material: "brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P)"} — alternatives? Could set alternatives null.
4. role: "reed sensor (ancillary device)", alternatives: "OR" with inductive, characteristics: {...}
5. role: "inductive sensor / inductive pulser (ancillary device)", alternatives: "OR", characteristics.

Hmm alternatives per component entry meaning that entry is one of OR alternatives. I'll set alternatives: "OR" on both sensor entries.

Characteristics struct: characteristics{} on components — the schema says components[] has characteristics{} — free object. OK.

Certificate-level:
- number: "R49/2013-A-CZ1-2021.07"
- scheme: "A"
- project_number: maybe "0511"? The type evaluation files start 0511. Not explicitly labeled project number. Omit.
- page_total: 7
- member_state: "Czech Republic"
- date_issued: "2022-09-27" (Revision 1 date). Original issue 2021-12-06. The certificate's current issue date is 27 September 2022. I'll use "2022-09-27".
- oiml_issuer_id: not given explicitly. Omit.

issuing_authority:
- name: "Czech Metrology Institute"
- address_lines: ["Okružní 31", "638 00 Brno", "Czech Republic"]
- person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra"
- person_title: omit? The signature block: "The OIML Issuing Authority RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body". Person responsible field is Jan Kalandra with no title. I'll set person_title: "Head of Certification Body"? That's Klenovský's title. Ambiguous. I'll omit person_title. Maybe include signatory in... schema doesn't have. Just person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra".
- website, phone, email: not present. Omit.
- oiml_issuer_id: omit.

certified_type:
- category: "Water meter" — the schema examples list categories like "Gas meter"; this is a water meter. Use "Water meter".
- type_designations: ["GKMV40", "GKMV40P"]
- module_designation: the doc shows "-" meaning not applicable → "Not applicable"
- description: "Positive displacement water meter with dry mechanical indicating device; brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P) body..." I'll compose concise description.

- id: "R49"
- edition: 2013
- amendment: null/omit
- scheme: "A"
- accuracy_classes: [2] — hmm as number 2? "2". I'll use [2]? The schema says accuracy_classes[]. Values — use strings? R49 class 2 is numeric-ish but class designations can be "2". I'll use ["2"]. Actually for water meters class is written as "2". I'll use [2]... safer as string "2"? Many classes like "Y" are strings. I'll use ["2"].

Wait, "Edition (year): 2013" → edition: 2013. The schema says edition (int). OK.

Matrix table: include one combining the per-DN data. Footnotes: none directly in that table.

Now the component list — decide final:

Maybe also body material as component: role "body", characteristics {material: "brass (GKMV40) or composite (GKMV40P)"}. I'll include it.
